newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Norwegian PM raises human rights with Vietnam.
newsitem.headline: Norwegian PM raises human rights with Vietnam.

text.p: Norwegian Prime Minister Gro Harlem Brundtland raised human rights concerns with Vietnam's leaders on Wednesday and said she had also discussed democratic development in the communist country.
Brundtland told a news conference in Hanoi she had presented her Vietnamese counterpart, Vo Van Kiet, with a list of concerns in a letter compiled by human rights group Amnesty International.
She declined to give details of its contents but said Hanoi had accepted the letter and agreed to look at the concerns.
Brundtland said she had also discussed freedom of speech issues and the development of democratic institutions in Vietnam, as well as improvements to the country's legal system.

"In China, in Vietnam, in certain other countries there is...a one party system. That does, however, not mean that those countries do not have considerable development into more open societies," she said.
Further details of her talks were not given.
Brundtland's three-day visit, the first by a Norwegian prime minister to Vietnam, has seen the signing of a range of technical and development assistance accords as well as the opening of an embassy.
Oslo normalised relations with Hanoi in 1971, four years before the Vietnam War ended. But until earlier this year its interests here were handled by its embassy in Bangkok.
The Scandinavian country ranks 32nd among foreign investors in Vietnam, with $23 million earmarked for four projects, and bilateral trade at around $20 million a year.
Brundtland was due to fly to Ho Chi Minh City, the country's southern economic hub, before departing on Thursday.
